title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: include or exclude default file path exclusions on Windows
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing Windows exclusion controls and Endpoint DLP licensing are supported. It distinguishes the planned Microsoft-managed list from existing exclusions and correctly leaves the new control's configuration and arrival default unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an Endpoint DLP control to include or exclude default file path exclusions on Windows.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention: Add control to include or exclude Default file paths exclusions for Windows

claims.claim: The roadmap says customers previously configured system-file inclusion or exclusion manually.
claims.quote: Previously customers would have system files either included or excluded manually configured.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes providing the exclusions by default with an option to include or exclude the paths.
claims.quote: With this feature there is now a capability to provide this by default and have the option of including or excluding those paths.

claims.claim: Microsoft manages the list to ensure accuracy and ease of management.

claims.claim: The existing Windows exclusions are at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.
claims.quote: To configure path exclusions in DLP settings, go to Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings @{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";} configures an administrator-entered exclusion.
claims.quote: The EndpointDlpGlobalSettings parameter specifies the global endpoints. ... Example values: ... @{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";}

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The documented PathExclusion example supplies an individual manual path rather than a switch for the Microsoft-managed list.
claims.quote: Example values: ... @{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";} ... @{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="%AppData%\Mozilla";}

claims.claim: Neither a Windows UI toggle nor an automation operation for including or excluding the Microsoft-managed list is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Set-PolicyConfig" "Windows" "default" "exclusions"; Endpoint DLP Windows Microsoft managed default file path exclusions include exclude toggle. Opened Configure endpoint data loss prevention settings and Set-PolicyConfig; no managed-list control.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "Windows" "default" "exclusions" "include". Read roadmap, Configure endpoint data loss prevention settings and Endpoint DLP support-table excerpts; none states the new Windows control's initial include/exclude choice.

claims.quote: To exclude certain paths from DLP monitoring, DLP alerts, and DLP policy enforcement on your devices, set up file path exclusions to turn off those configuration settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The contents of the new Microsoft-managed Windows exclusion list have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Endpoint DLP" "Windows" "default" "exclusions" "include"; "Purview" "default file path exclusions" "Windows" "toggle". Read roadmap and Configure endpoint data loss prevention settings; neither identifies the new list's contents.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap does not describe how or when Microsoft changes the list over time.
claims.quote: Searched: the entire supplied roadmap description for update frequency, automatic changes and announcements. It says Microsoft manages the list, but does not describe how or when its contents change.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not say how an administrator views the list's contents.
claims.quote: Searched: the entire supplied roadmap description for viewing or inspecting the list. It describes providing default paths and the include/exclude choice, but no way to view the list.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no performance information about excluding the Microsoft-managed list.
claims.quote: Searched: the entire supplied roadmap description for performance effects of excluding the list. It describes manual configuration, default paths, an include/exclude option and Microsoft management, without performance information.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a path-exclusion setting without describing new data access or permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: the entire supplied roadmap description for data access, identity and permissions. It discusses only system-file exclusions, providing default paths, the include/exclude choice and Microsoft managing the list.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no autonomous actions beyond saying that Microsoft manages the list.
claims.quote: Searched: the entire supplied roadmap description for autonomous actions. It describes an administrator's include/exclude choice and states: 'This list is managed by Microsoft to ensure accuracy and ease of management.'

claims.claim: Which roles can change the new managed-list control is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP permissions roles manage endpoint settings file path exclusions. Read endpoint settings, Set-PolicyConfig, Purview permissions and Create and deploy DLP policies; none states roles for the new control.

claims.claim: Activity explorer is a place to check audit activity from onboarded Endpoint DLP devices.
claims.quote: Once a device is onboarded, it should be visible in the devices list, and should start reporting audit activity to Activity explorer.

claims.claim: The Set-PolicyConfig reference gives individual PathExclusion entries as its example values.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; writer evidence
claims.claim: The roadmap does not explain the new list's interaction with administrator-entered exclusions.
claims.quote: Previously customers would have system files either included or excluded manually configured. With this feature there is now a capability to provide this by default and have the option of including or excluding those paths.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; writer evidence
claims.claim: The roadmap does not state that excluding the Microsoft-managed list restores monitoring for particular system paths.
claims.quote: Searched: the entire supplied roadmap description for restored monitoring and enforcement after excluding the managed list. It says there is an option of including or excluding the paths, without describing the resulting monitoring coverage.
